key_insight: Proximity to a metal-insulator transition can be used to tune correlated-oxide transparent conductors so they become more transparent without completely losing useful conductivity.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical design rule for transparent electrodes in optoelectronic and solar devices, especially when targeting the visible-to-silicon-photovoltaic spectral range.
method: Use epitaxial Ti-substituted SrVO3 films as a model correlated oxide platform.
Tune composition to move the material toward the metal-insulator transition.
Evaluate the transparency-conductivity trade-off with Haacke figure-of-merit analysis and electronic-structure signatures.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a systematically widened optical window, but also reduced carrier density and coherence near the composition-driven MIT, with the best figure-of-merit found near that transition.
watch_item: Approaching the MIT improves transparency but can introduce disorder and carrier depletion that degrade metallic transport, so composition control must be very precise.
paper_title: Engineering Correlated Transparent Conductors via Metal-Insulator Transition Proximity
